Gold falls below $4,000 as dollar surges, Fed hike bets rise - Kitco PM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold prices were lower and spot silver prices were modestly higher in late U.S. trading Wednesday, as a stronger U.S. dollar and expectations for additional Federal Reserve interest rate increases continued to pressure bullion following Tuesday's hotter-than-expected inflation report. Gold surrendered its early gains and fell below $4,000.00 an ounce, while silver attracted some buying interest despite the restrictive monetary policy outlook. Rising crude oil prices, renewed uncertainty surrounding the Strait of Hormuz and a broad recovery in global equity markets provided competing influences on precious metals. Spot gold was trading near $3,983.20 an ounce, down $48.60, or 1.21%, while spot silver was trading near $51.560 an ounce, up $0.149, or 0.29%, on the session.. Tuesday's U.S. consumer price index showed headline inflation increasing 0.4% in October, exceeding expectations for a 0.3% gain, while core prices rose 0.3%, also above forecasts. Shelter costs increased 0.3%, food prices advanced 0.5% and energy prices rose 0.7%, indicating persistent price pressure across several categories. The Bureau of Labor Statistics did not publish annual October inflation rates because comparable observations for October 2025 were unavailable following the federal government shutdown. The inflation surprise followed Friday's stronger-than-expected employment report, which showed 165,000 new jobs in October, a decline in unemployment to 4.1% and monthly average hourly earnings growth of 0.4%. The combination of resilient employment and persistent inflation has strengthened expectations for further Fed tightening.

items.titleEn: Gold miners enjoy strong Q2 despite lower gold price, higher expenses and operational disruptions – WGC's Blagden
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – While the second quarter of the year saw gold prices pull back dramatically from the all-time highs of Q1, and rising expenses and operational disruptions ate into margins and profitability, gold miners still enjoyed an excellent Q2 by annual and historical measures, according to a new analysis by Oliver Blagden, Mine Supply Analyst at Metals Focus on behalf of the World Gold Council (WGC). After seeing an exceptional first quarter in 2026, Blagden wrote that lower gold prices combined with increased costs to put miners’ margins under additional pressure. “Global average gold producer All-In Sustaining Costs (AISC) rose by 8% q/q and 22% y/y to a record US$1,930/oz,” he noted. “This marked the 29th consecutive year-on-year increase, underlining the persistence of cost pressures. Higher sustaining capital expenditure, operating expenses and production disruption outweighed lower royalties, although strong cash generation continued to support investment, shareholder returns and resilient balance sheets.”

items.titleEn: Gold prices fall below $4,000 as analysts warn of further losses toward $3,900
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Gold prices have fallen below the critical $4,000-an-ounce level, and analysts warn that the precious metal could face further selling pressure as persistent inflation forces the Federal Reserve to maintain its tightening bias. Although gold managed to hold support around $4,000 for the past two weeks, the latest selling pressure threatens to undermine the market's recent recovery. Analysts warn that a sustained break below this critical pivot point could trigger another wave of liquidation. Spot gold last traded at $3,987 an ounce, down more than 1% on the day. In a report published Tuesday, Bark Melek, Head of Commodity Strategy at TD Securities, said he expects gold prices to retest support near $3,900 an ounce as higher interest rates and a stronger U.S. dollar continue to weigh on investment demand.

items.titleEn: BMO says silver's solar boom is fading, investment demand unlikely to compensate
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Growing fears that rising inflation will force the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates aggressively next month are weighing on gold , with the yellow metal down more than 1% on the day. However, silver is significantly outperforming, with prices holding above $51 an ounce, up 0.68% on the day. Although the gold-silver ratio is falling, one bank expects the overall trend to remain higher as silver’s industrial demand continues to weaken. In a new report, the commodity team at BMO Capital Markets, led by George Heppel and Helen Amos, said that the gold-silver ratio has embarked on a structural uptrend and is expected to trade around 85 points over the next four years, up from 76 points currently.
